title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a lemma in commutative algebra feeding a concrete search. Grothendieck wants to classify double covers of P^1_Z (equivalently of the affine line E^1_Z = Spec Z[t]) that are generically smooth over Spec Z, i.e. generically étale on every fibre. His motivation, visible on the neighbouring pages, is to build étale covers of P^1_Z minus {0, λ, ∞}, with λ = 2^α 3^β the exceptional modular invariant, for the moduli of elliptic curves.

(1) Local lemma. Let A be a local ring with maximal ideal m, residue field k and residue characteristic p. Let B = A[S]/(S^2 - a). The application only uses A = Z[t] localized at the prime pZ[t], which is a DVR, so the lemma should be read with A a DVR. Over a DVR, B is one-dimensional and free with basis 1, S, and 'normal' coincides with 'regular'.

(2) Case p ≠ 2. B is normal iff a ∉ m^2. Necessity holds in every characteristic: if a = π^2 c, then S/π is integral over B but does not lie in B.

(3) Case p = 2.
- (a) a ∈ m: B is local with maximal ideal (m, S), and B is normal iff a ∉ m^2.
- (b1) a is a unit and its image ȧ is not a square in k: B is a DVR with residue field k(√ȧ).
- (b2) ȧ = α̇^2. Lift α̇ to a unit α and write a = α^2 - b with b ∈ m. Substituting T = S - α gives S^2 - a = T^2 + 2αT + b. Since 2 ∈ m, the completion of B is Â[[T]]/(T^2 + 2αT + b). Because T^2 and 2αT lie in m_C^2, B is regular iff b ∉ m^2.
- The class of b in m/m^2 does not depend on the choice of α: replacing α by α + μ changes b by 2αμ + μ^2, which lies in m^2.

(4) Summary of the normal cases: a ∈ m \ m^2; or a = α^2 - b with α a unit and b ∈ m \ m^2; or a a unit with ȧ ∉ k^2. Equivalently, B fails to be normal iff a ∈ m^2, or (p = 2 and a is congruent mod m^2 to the square of a unit). Two further margin notes:
- in the normal cases B is regular;
- for p ≠ 2, B is local iff a ∈ m or ȧ ∉ k^2.
Over Z_(2) this is the classical rule that Z[√d] is 2-maximal iff d ≢ 1 mod 4 (d squarefree).

(5) Global set-up. The double cover over the generic point is a quadratic extension of Q(t), so it is given by a class in Q(t)^*/Q(t)^{*2}. A basis of this F_2-space consists of -1, the primes p, and the primitive irreducible polynomials of Z[t] with positive leading coefficient. Hence each class has a unique representative P = ±qQ, with q a squarefree natural number and Q in Z[t] primitive, squarefree in Q[t], with positive leading coefficient.

(6) Next step (previous and next pages). Applying the lemma at each height-one prime pZ[t]:
- generic étaleness on the fibres forces q = 1;
- since S^2 - P is never generically étale in characteristic 2, one needs εQ to be a square mod 4, which fixes the sign ε;
- example: Q = T(T - λ) with 4 | λ.
errors: The opening hypothesis, read as 'A régulier', makes the claim false in dimension ≥ 2. 'B normal iff a ∉ m^2' is then wrong: S^2 = xy over k[x,y] localized gives a normal A_1 singularity with a ∈ m^2. In general the criterion characterizes regularity of B, not normality. It is correct as stated only for A a DVR, which is the case actually used (Z[t] localized at pZ[t]).

The completion should be written Â[[T]]/(f), not A[[T]]/(f). Also, the identification of the completion of B with this quotient uses that B is local in case b2 (true, since S^2 - ȧ = (S - α̇)^2 mod m) plus Weierstrass preparation. Both points are minor.
The F_2-basis of Q(t)^*/Q(t)^{*2} listed in a), b) omits -1, although the ± sign is restored in formula (1).
Notational slips: 'Z_p[t]' should be F_p[t]; 'Q(t)/Q(t)^*' should be Q(t)^*/Q(t)^{*2}; on the previous page, 'normalisé de E'_Z' should read E^1_Z.

ideas.what: Criterion for regularity/normality of a quadratic extension A[S]/(S^2-a) of a DVR, including residue characteristic 2, via completing the square a = α^2 - b and testing b mod m^2
ideas.modern_name: Maximal orders / normalization of quadratic extensions; ramification of quadratic extensions in residue characteristic 2 (Artin–Schreier-type reduction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Dedekind for quadratic fields; general DVR version standard, e.g. Serre's Corps locaux and textbook treatments)
ideas.where_published: Normality/regularity criteria in EGA IV in general form; this explicit computation not known to be in Grothendieck's texts

ideas.what: Description of quadratic extensions of Q(t) by squarefree representatives ±qQ (q squarefree integer, Q primitive squarefree polynomial)
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory for Q(t)^*/Q(t)^{*2}; Gauss lemma / UFD structure of Z[t]

ideas.what: Program of classifying double covers of P^1_Z that are generically étale on all fibres, to produce étale covers of P^1_Z minus {0, 1728, ∞} related to the moduli of elliptic curves
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} over Z / covers of P^1_Z minus three points; cf. modular functions such as sqrt(j-1728) = E6/sqrt(Δ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Context of Grothendieck's anabelian/Teichmüller program; arithmetic of modular curves (Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and π_1 over Q in general terms, not this computation

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but classical computation: normality of S^2 = a over a DVR, generalizing the d ≡ 1 mod 4 phenomenon, plus a standard Kummer-theoretic parametrization. It serves a concrete search for étale double covers of P^1_Z minus points. Nothing here is new or absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2, 'On suppose d'abord A anneau [?] régulier [?]': the qualifier is barely legible. The mathematics (normal ⇔ regular, 'B normal ssi a ∉ m²') only holds if A is a DVR / regular of dimension 1, which matches the application to A_{pA}.

Left margin (lower): this note most likely reads 'B non normal ssi a ∈ m², ou a mod m² est le carré d'une unité de A/m². Ce dernier cas correspond ...', i.e. it describes the NON-normal cases (b ∈ m²), not the normal ones.
In b), 'P mod p ∈ Z_p[t]' means F_p[t] (Grothendieck's notation Z_p = Z/pZ).
Under the basis list the conditions read: 'a_0 > 0, les a_i premiers entre eux (i.e. ∀p ∈ P, P mod p ≠ 0 dans Z_p[t]), P premier dans Q[T]'.
Top margin: 'NB Si p≠2, alors B est local ssi a ∈ m ou (a ∉ m et) ȧ ∉ k²'.
